attacks.claim: Zero-config auto-loading executes any package under node_modules carrying the `tasq-plugin` keyword (including transitive or typosquatted ones) on every invocation, with no allowlist or trust step. Discovery runs before argument parsing, so even `--version`, CI, editor integrations and pre-commit hooks run third-party code. The supply-chain section (provenance, no postinstall) does not address this trust-boundary expansion.
attacks.evidence: "Any installed package with the `tasq-plugin` keyword is picked up automatically." / "Discovery runs before argument parsing so that plugins can register subcommands."

attacks.claim: The glob `**/node_modules/**/package.json` matches every nested package.json, including files inside packages (fixtures, nested node_modules, workspace copies). Plugins are found at any depth, so duplicates and unintended transitive packages can be loaded. There is no filter to top-level installed packages or to the declared dependency set.

The performance claim contradicts the artifact's own table. Discovery adds about 1.8 s per invocation: `--version` goes 0.11→1.94 s, lint-staged 0.38→2.31 s, cache-hit 0.21→2.02 s. These are 5-10x regressions on the exact hot paths the docs recommend (pre-commit, CI, editors). The text calls the cost 'negligible' and claims overall build time improves, and the 'under 50 ms' cache claim is not what users will experience.
attacks.evidence: | `tasq run build` (cache hit) | 0.21 s | 2.02 s | ... "Discovery is a fixed per-invocation cost and becomes negligible relative to real build work"

attacks.claim: Discovery is an unbounded full-tree walk on every invocation with no cache, depth limit or ignore list. Its cost grows with installed package count: 2,430 packages already costs about 1.8 s, and larger monorepos will be worse. This makes pre-commit hooks and editor integrations noticeably slow.
attacks.evidence: for await (const pkgJson of glob("**/node_modules/**/package.json", ...)) — no depth limit, cache, or ignore list

attacks.claim: The `plugins` config array is silently ignored, not rejected or warned about, and `tasq-migrate` installs nothing new. Existing plugins whose packages lack the keyword stop loading with no error. Yarn PnP projects, which have no node_modules, find no plugins either, and nothing says how that is surfaced.
attacks.evidence: `plugins` array in config ignored | Auto-discovery replaces it; `tasq-migrate` removes the array and installs nothing new

attacks.claim: `discoverPlugins` has no error handling. One malformed package.json makes JSON.parse throw and aborts every invocation, including pre-commit hooks that would then block commits. There is no timeout or diagnostics, and the plan defines no P1 criteria or monitoring for the 7-day `next` window.
attacks.evidence: const pkg = JSON.parse(await readFile(join(root, pkgJson), "utf8")); — no try/catch; "promote to `latest` after 7 days with no P1 issues"

attacks.claim: The rollback via dist-tag does not revert configs already rewritten by `tasq-migrate`, or code executed by auto-loaded plugins. It is otherwise a reasonable, reversible plan.
The license scan statement covers only the two new runtime deps and does not say whether transitive dependencies are included.
The grouped pretty reporter's plain-text and screen-reader behaviour is unspecified.
